name: Austurvöllur
description: A small grassy square in the centre, facing the Parliament building and the cathedral, with a statue of the independence leader Jón Sigurðsson.

name: Harpa
description: The glass-fronted concert hall on the harbour, opened in 2011 and home of the Iceland Symphony Orchestra.

name: Lækjartorg
description: A small square in the city centre, where Lækjargata meets Austurstræti, long used as a meeting point and for public gatherings.

name: Hallgrímskirkja
description: The concrete Lutheran church on the hill above the centre, with a 74.5 m tower you can go up. A statue of Leif Erikson stands in front.

name: University of Iceland
description: Iceland’s oldest and largest university, founded in 1911, on a campus just south of the city centre next to the National Museum.

name: Kaffibarinn
description: A small downtown bar in an old house just off Laugavegur, a fixture of the city’s nightlife since the 1990s and a setting in the film 101 Reykjavík.

name: Höfði House
description: A white wooden house by the shore, built in 1909, where the US and Soviet leaders Reagan and Gorbachev held their 1986 summit.

name: Laugardalshöll
description: The city’s main indoor sports and concert hall, where the 1972 world chess championship between Fischer and Spassky was played.

name: Icelandic Phallological Museum
description: A museum devoted to penises, with a large collection of specimens from Iceland’s land and sea mammals, in the Hafnartorg development by the harbour.
